description: FoundryTrade business knowledge for the AI Database Agent (V4). Definitions, conventions and 'not tracked' notes are what a data team would write in a metrics glossary; examples are verified question/SQL pairs. Retrieved per question and added to the prompt. Never copy benchmark questions (eval/questions.json) into this file.

entries.title: Revenue (net sales)
entries.text: Revenue is the sum of sales.OrderLines.LineTotal for orders whose Status is not 'Cancelled' or 'Returned'. LineTotal already applies the line discount. Shipping fees are not revenue. Attribute revenue to the period of the order's OrderDate.
entries.sql: SELECT SUM(l.LineTotal) AS Revenue FROM sales.Orders o JOIN sales.OrderLines l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId WHERE o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')

entries.title: Gross bookings
entries.text: Gross bookings (gross sales) is the value of everything ordered: sum of LineTotal for all orders except 'Cancelled', including orders later returned. Use it only when the question says bookings or gross sales; otherwise use revenue.

entries.title: Average order value (AOV)
entries.text: Average order value is revenue per order: first total each order's LineTotal (revenue rule: exclude Cancelled and Returned orders), then average those order totals. Never average individual order lines — an order has several lines.
entries.sql: SELECT AVG(t.OrderRevenue) AS AverageOrderValue FROM (SELECT o.OrderId, SUM(l.LineTotal) AS OrderRevenue FROM sales.Orders o JOIN sales.OrderLines l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId WHERE o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned') GROUP BY o.OrderId) AS t

entries.title: Units sold
entries.text: Units sold is SUM(sales.OrderLines.Quantity) over orders that count as revenue (not Cancelled or Returned).

entries.title: Gross margin and gross profit
entries.text: Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold, where cost of goods sold = OrderLines.Quantity × catalog.Products.UnitCost. Gross margin % = gross profit / revenue × 100. Use the revenue rule for which orders count. UnitCost is today's cost, so historical margins are an approximation.
entries.sql: SELECT SUM(l.LineTotal) - SUM(l.Quantity * p.UnitCost) AS GrossProfit, 100.0 * (SUM(l.LineTotal) - SUM(l.Quantity * p.UnitCost)) / NULLIF(SUM(l.LineTotal), 0) AS GrossMarginPct FROM sales.Orders o JOIN sales.OrderLines l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId JOIN catalog.Products p ON p.ProductId = l.ProductId WHERE o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')

entries.title: Number of orders placed
entries.text: 'Orders placed' counts every order by OrderDate regardless of Status (cancelled orders were still placed). Filter by Status only when the question asks for a particular status, or for orders that count as revenue.

entries.title: Calendar periods: last month, this year, quarters
entries.text: Periods are calendar periods relative to today's date, not rolling windows. 'Last month' is the whole previous calendar month; 'this month' is the current calendar month to date; 'last year' is the previous calendar year; 'this year' or 'year to date' runs from 1 January of the current year to today; quarters are Q1 Jan–Mar, Q2 Apr–Jun, Q3 Jul–Sep, Q4 Oct–Dec. Use half-open ranges (>= start AND < next start). Only say 'last 30 days' style rolling windows when the question does. Previous calendar month start: DATEADD(month, DATEDIFF(month, 0, GETDATE()) - 1, 0); current month start: DATEADD(month, DATEDIFF(month, 0, GETDATE()), 0); current year start: DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(GETDATE()), 1, 1).

entries.title: Data coverage and cut-off
entries.text: Orders run from 2023-01-01 to 2026-08-31. Nothing is recorded after 31 August 2026, so periods after that date (for example September 2026) contain no orders; say so rather than guessing.

entries.title: Growth and year-over-year comparisons
entries.text: Growth % = (current period value − comparison period value) / comparison period value × 100. Year-over-year compares the same calendar period one year earlier (for example July 2026 vs July 2025). Compute each period's value separately (conditional aggregation or two CTEs), then the percentage.

entries.title: Top-level categories and the category tree
entries.text: Products belong to subcategories (catalog.Categories rows with a ParentCategoryId). Top-level categories (Power Tools, Hand Tools, Fasteners & Hardware, Safety Equipment, Workshop Storage) have ParentCategoryId NULL. To report by top-level category, join the product's category to its parent and group by COALESCE(parent, self): JOIN catalog.Categories c ON c.CategoryId = p.CategoryId JOIN catalog.Categories tc ON tc.CategoryId = COALESCE(c.ParentCategoryId, c.CategoryId), then GROUP BY tc.Name. 'Category' on its own usually means the subcategory a product is assigned to.

entries.title: Customer spend and top customers
entries.text: How much a customer spent or generated is revenue attributed to their orders (revenue rule), not the sum of payments — payments lag orders and include refunds.

entries.title: Showing customer names
entries.text: Business customers (Segment SmallBusiness or Enterprise) have a CompanyName; consumers do not. Display COALESCE(c.CompanyName, CONCAT(c.FirstName, ' ', c.LastName)) and include CustomerId when names may repeat.

entries.title: Active and new customers
entries.text: An active customer has at least one order that is not Cancelled with an OrderDate in the 12 months before today. A new customer in a period is one whose sales.Customers.CreatedAt falls in that period. Customers who never ordered exist.

entries.title: Return rate and cancellation rate
entries.text: Return rate % = orders with Status 'Returned' / orders that were shipped (Status 'Shipped', 'Delivered' or 'Returned') × 100. Cancellation rate % = orders with Status 'Cancelled' / all orders placed × 100. Multiply by 100.0 (not 100) to avoid integer division.

entries.title: Fulfilment (shipping) time
entries.text: Fulfilment time is ShippedDate − OrderDate for orders that have a ShippedDate. Measure in hours with DATEDIFF(hour, OrderDate, ShippedDate); for days use DATEDIFF(hour, ...) / 24.0 so averages keep fractions (DATEDIFF(day, ...) counts midnights and AVG of ints truncates).

entries.title: Shipping fees and total charged
entries.text: sales.Orders.ShippingFee is charged per order and is not part of revenue. The total a customer is charged for an order is the order's LineTotal sum plus ShippingFee.

entries.title: Payments, refunds and net payments
entries.text: sales.Payments has one payment per paid order and, for returned orders, a refund row with IsRefund = 1 and a negative Amount. Payments received excludes refunds (IsRefund = 0); refunded total is the sum of refund amounts (report as a positive number unless asked otherwise); net payments = SUM(Amount) over all rows.

entries.title: Unpaid orders and amount outstanding
entries.text: An order is unpaid when it has no row in sales.Payments with IsRefund = 0. Amount outstanding for an unpaid, non-cancelled order is its LineTotal sum plus ShippingFee. Invoice customers pay 14–45 days after ordering, so recent invoice orders are often unpaid.

entries.title: Sales reps and web orders
entries.text: Sales reps are employees in the Sales department (hr.EmployeeDirectory joined to hr.Departments where Name = 'Sales'), linked to orders by sales.Orders.SalesRepId. Orders with SalesRepId NULL were placed on the website without a rep. Sales rep performance uses the revenue rule for revenue and counts all orders for 'orders handled'.

entries.title: Employees, headcount and reporting lines
entries.text: hr.EmployeeDirectory lists staff. Current employees have TerminationDate NULL; headcount means current employees. ManagerId is the EmployeeId of the direct manager (self-join the directory to get the manager's name); the CEO has no manager. Job titles are in JobTitle, departments via DepartmentId.

entries.title: Inventory value
entries.text: Inventory value at cost = SUM(inventory.Stock.QuantityOnHand × catalog.Products.UnitCost); at list (retail) price = SUM(QuantityOnHand × ListPrice). Stock is held per warehouse per product; total stock of a product sums its warehouses.

entries.title: Stock-outs and reorder level
entries.text: A product is out of stock in a warehouse when inventory.Stock.QuantityOnHand = 0, and below reorder level when QuantityOnHand < ReorderLevel. ReorderLevel is on inventory.Stock (per warehouse), not on catalog.Products. 'Out of stock everywhere' means no warehouse has QuantityOnHand > 0.

entries.title: Active and discontinued products
entries.text: catalog.Products.IsDiscontinued = 1 marks products no longer sold; active products have IsDiscontinued = 0. LaunchedOn is when a product was first offered; products launched in 2024–2025 are 'new products'.

entries.title: Warehouses and regions
entries.text: Orders ship from one of four warehouses: Chicago Hub (United States, Canada), Leeds Depot (United Kingdom, Ireland), Rotterdam Central (continental Europe) and Singapore East (Singapore, Australia, New Zealand). sales.Orders.WarehouseId says where an order shipped from; ShipCountry where it went.

entries.title: Suppliers and lead times
entries.text: Each product has one supplier (catalog.Products.SupplierId). LeadTimeDays is the typical delivery time from that supplier. Purchase orders to suppliers are not recorded.

entries.title: Not tracked: website analytics
entries.text: FoundryTrade's database has no website analytics: no sessions, visits, page views, traffic sources, conversion rates, carts or cart abandonment. Questions about these cannot be answered from this data. (Web orders are only identifiable as orders with SalesRepId NULL — that is not a conversion rate.)

entries.title: Not tracked: marketing and advertising
entries.text: There is no data on marketing spend, campaigns, advertising, promotions budgets, customer acquisition cost or return on ad spend. Questions about these cannot be answered.

entries.title: Not available: salaries and compensation
entries.text: Employee salaries, bonuses and any compensation are confidential and not available to this agent. Questions about pay, salary or who earns the most cannot be answered.

entries.title: Not stored: customer phone numbers and addresses
entries.text: Customers have only an email address, city and country. Phone numbers, postal addresses and contact persons are not stored.

entries.title: Not tracked: reviews, returns reasons, purchase history, cost history
entries.text: There are no product reviews or ratings, no reasons for returns or cancellations, no purchase orders to suppliers, no historical cost or price lists (only current UnitCost and ListPrice), and no customer support tickets.

entries.title: Gross margin % by subcategory in 2025
entries.question: What was the gross margin percentage for each product subcategory in 2025?
entries.text: Gross margin % per subcategory for 2025 orders that count as revenue.
entries.sql:
SELECT c.Name AS Subcategory,
       CAST(100.0 * (SUM(l.LineTotal) - SUM(l.Quantity * p.UnitCost)) / NULLIF(SUM(l.LineTotal), 0) AS decimal(5, 2)) AS GrossMarginPct
FROM sales.Orders AS o
JOIN sales.OrderLines AS l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId
JOIN catalog.Products AS p ON p.ProductId = l.ProductId
JOIN catalog.Categories AS c ON c.CategoryId = p.CategoryId
WHERE o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND o.OrderDate >= '2025-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY c.Name
ORDER BY GrossMarginPct DESC;

entries.title: Year-over-year revenue growth by country
entries.question: How did revenue in each ship country change from 2024 to 2025, in percent?
entries.text: Revenue per ship country in 2024 and 2025 and the growth percentage.
entries.sql:
SELECT o.ShipCountry,
       SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(o.OrderDate) = 2024 THEN l.LineTotal ELSE 0 END) AS Revenue2024,
       SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(o.OrderDate) = 2025 THEN l.LineTotal ELSE 0 END) AS Revenue2025,
       CAST(100.0 * (SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(o.OrderDate) = 2025 THEN l.LineTotal ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(o.OrderDate) = 2024 THEN l.LineTotal ELSE 0 END))
            / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN YEAR(o.OrderDate) = 2024 THEN l.LineTotal ELSE 0 END), 0) AS decimal(7, 2)) AS GrowthPct
FROM sales.Orders AS o
JOIN sales.OrderLines AS l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId
WHERE o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND o.OrderDate >= '2024-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY o.ShipCountry
ORDER BY GrowthPct DESC;

entries.title: Customers with unpaid orders
entries.question: Which customers have unpaid orders, and how much do they owe?
entries.text: Amount outstanding per customer: unpaid, non-cancelled orders' line totals plus shipping.
entries.sql:
WITH unpaid AS (
    SELECT o.OrderId, o.CustomerId, SUM(l.LineTotal) + o.ShippingFee AS AmountDue
    FROM sales.Orders AS o
    JOIN sales.OrderLines AS l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId
    WHERE o.Status <> 'Cancelled'
      AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales.Payments AS p WHERE p.OrderId = o.OrderId AND p.IsRefund = 0)
    GROUP BY o.OrderId, o.CustomerId, o.ShippingFee
)
SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(c.CompanyName, CONCAT(c.FirstName, ' ', c.LastName)) AS Customer,
       COUNT(*) AS UnpaidOrders, SUM(u.AmountDue) AS AmountDue
FROM unpaid AS u
JOIN sales.Customers AS c ON c.CustomerId = u.CustomerId
GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.CompanyName, c.FirstName, c.LastName
ORDER BY AmountDue DESC;

entries.title: Top sales reps by revenue this year
entries.question: Who are the top 3 sales reps by revenue this year?
entries.text: Revenue per sales rep from 1 January of the current year to today.
entries.sql:
SELECT TOP (3) e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName, SUM(l.LineTotal) AS Revenue
FROM sales.Orders AS o
JOIN sales.OrderLines AS l ON l.OrderId = o.OrderId
JOIN hr.EmployeeDirectory AS e ON e.EmployeeId = o.SalesRepId
WHERE o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND o.OrderDate >= DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(GETDATE()), 1, 1)
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
ORDER BY Revenue DESC;

entries.title: Headcount per manager
entries.question: How many current employees does each manager have as direct reports?
entries.text: Direct reports per manager, current employees only, using a self-join of the directory.
entries.sql:
SELECT m.EmployeeId, m.FirstName, m.LastName, m.JobTitle, COUNT(*) AS DirectReports
FROM hr.EmployeeDirectory AS e
JOIN hr.EmployeeDirectory AS m ON m.EmployeeId = e.ManagerId
WHERE e.TerminationDate IS NULL
GROUP BY m.EmployeeId, m.FirstName, m.LastName, m.JobTitle
ORDER BY DirectReports DESC;

entries.title: Out-of-stock products by warehouse
entries.question: Which active products are out of stock, and where?
entries.text: Active products with zero units on hand, per warehouse.
entries.sql:
SELECT w.Name AS Warehouse, p.Sku, p.Name AS Product
FROM inventory.Stock AS s
JOIN inventory.Warehouses AS w ON w.WarehouseId = s.WarehouseId
JOIN catalog.Products AS p ON p.ProductId = s.ProductId
WHERE s.QuantityOnHand = 0 AND p.IsDiscontinued = 0
ORDER BY w.Name, p.Name;

entries.title: Average fulfilment time by warehouse
entries.question: How many days does each warehouse take on average to ship an order?
entries.text: Average hours from order to shipment per warehouse, shown in days with fractions.
entries.sql:
SELECT w.Name AS Warehouse, CAST(AVG(DATEDIFF(hour, o.OrderDate, o.ShippedDate) / 24.0) AS decimal(6, 2)) AS AvgDaysToShip
FROM sales.Orders AS o
JOIN inventory.Warehouses AS w ON w.WarehouseId = o.WarehouseId
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY w.Name
ORDER BY AvgDaysToShip;

entries.title: Payments and refunds by method
entries.question: For each payment method, how much was received, refunded and kept in 2025?
entries.text: Payments received, refunds (as positive numbers) and net per method for 2025.
entries.sql:
SELECT p.Method,
       SUM(CASE WHEN p.IsRefund = 0 THEN p.Amount ELSE 0 END) AS Received,
       -SUM(CASE WHEN p.IsRefund = 1 THEN p.Amount ELSE 0 END) AS Refunded,
       SUM(p.Amount) AS Net
FROM sales.Payments AS p
WHERE p.PaidAt >= '2025-01-01' AND p.PaidAt < '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY p.Method
ORDER BY Net DESC;

entries.title: Customers who stopped ordering
entries.question: Which business customers ordered in 2024 but not in 2025?
entries.text: Business customers with a non-cancelled 2024 order and no non-cancelled 2025 order.
entries.sql:
SELECT c.CustomerId, c.CompanyName, c.Segment
FROM sales.Customers AS c
WHERE c.Segment <> 'Consumer'
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales.Orders AS o WHERE o.CustomerId = c.CustomerId AND o.Status <> 'Cancelled' AND o.OrderDate >= '2024-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2025-01-01')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales.Orders AS o WHERE o.CustomerId = c.CustomerId AND o.Status <> 'Cancelled' AND o.OrderDate >= '2025-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2026-01-01')
ORDER BY c.CompanyName;

entries.title: Sales of newly launched products
entries.question: How many units of products launched in 2024 or later have we sold, per product?
entries.text: Units sold per product launched on or after 1 January 2024.
entries.sql:
SELECT p.Sku, p.Name, p.LaunchedOn, SUM(l.Quantity) AS UnitsSold
FROM catalog.Products AS p
JOIN sales.OrderLines AS l ON l.ProductId = p.ProductId
JOIN sales.Orders AS o ON o.OrderId = l.OrderId
WHERE p.LaunchedOn >= '2024-01-01'
  AND o.Status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
GROUP BY p.Sku, p.Name, p.LaunchedOn
ORDER BY UnitsSold DESC;
